answer: Vouch edges: each answer must cite an earlier answer from a different identity and be checked against it, so every submission adds a public edge to a shared dependency graph. A farm cannot pool one history across clones: edges inside a sybil cluster bunch into a dense clique that samplers flag. To pass it must buy edges from outside, and those holders charge more as the cluster grows, so cost rises faster than head count. Honest work accumulates like nectar; a bought graph collapses in the first gale of sampling. What remains is scarce as saffron.
